summary.text: 门 is the simplified form of 門, “gate” or “door.” 門 is understood as a picture of a gate with paired leaves, though whether it began as one gate image or as two 戶 remains disputed.

formation.text: The traditional graph 門 is pictographic: it represents a gate with opposing leaves, sometimes shown with a lintel. A competing analysis treats it as two 戶, or door leaves; the original construction is unresolved.

components.text: This whole graph is interpreted as a gate with opposing leaves, sometimes with a lintel. The analysis as two 戶 is one account; another treats 門 as a single gate picture.

history.text: 門 is indexed in oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript and Small Seal forms. The curated oracle-bone-style image shows paired uprights and crossbars; it illustrates the gate interpretation but does not establish a sequence of graphic changes.
门 is identified as the simplified counterpart of 門; the specific graphic changes are not described.

uncertainties.text: The traditional graph is analyzed either as a whole gate picture or as two 戶; a further analysis calls it a semantic compound. The accounts do not resolve the original design.
The reported early gate examples and later uses do not establish an exact first attestation or a dated sequence of meanings.

senses.period: oracle-bone corpus examples; exact dating unresolved
senses.text: Oracle-bone corpus examples are reported using 門 for gates, including a temple gate and a hall gate. These attest the gate meaning but do not establish the graph’s first occurrence.
A verbal use meaning “to attack a city gate” is reported. Its relation to the gate noun and its chronology are unresolved.
Uses meaning “path” or “key point” are reported, but their chronology and connection to the gate sense are unresolved.
Uses meaning “lineage” or “category” are reported, but their chronology and semantic path from the gate sense are unresolved.
Current glosses include “gate,” “door,” “entrance,” and “opening”; these glosses do not establish a chronology among the meanings.

developments.text: A verbal use is reported alongside the gate noun, but no historical transition is established.
A connection to the gate sense is plausible, but no semantic development is established.
The reported uses are not linked to the gate sense by an established historical transition.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish an exact earliest attestation or a dated chronology for later senses.

items.period: Shang period script style, traditionally dated broadly to the late second millennium BCE; this is a modern redraw, not an artifact photograph
items.caption: An oracle-bone-style form of 門 has two tall uprights crossed by horizontal bars, giving the appearance of paired gate leaves. Paleographic accounts analyze the graph as two 戶, while its original design remains disputed.
items.alt: Black drawing of two tall uprights, each crossed by horizontal bars, forming a gate-like shape.
items.selection_reason: The visible form offers a clear example of the gate imagery central to the competing explanations of 門.

limitations.text: This is a modern redraw in an oracle-bone style, not an ancient artifact. The evidence supports a paired-leaf interpretation but does not settle whether 門 began as a whole gate picture or as two 戶.
